fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low visibility or at night can locate it without delay.
• Trim back dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain a clear path for emergency vehicles from the road to the residence.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency equipment can reach the front of the residence without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation that contacts or overhangs the main residence and detached structure to reduce the chance of fire spreading between plants and buildings.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure to allow responders to move around it on foot without obstruction.
• Install a gate latch or lock box on perimeter fencing that responders can open quickly without forcing entry.
• Mark any pedestrian gate in the perimeter fencing with a reflective indicator so responders can locate it at night.
• Keep a clear path along the walkway between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• If the rear of the property has no vehicle access, identify and mark the best pedestrian route from the front driveway to the rear for responders arriving on foot.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Brush Area; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Long Driveway; Grass Cover; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Green Space; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin trees within the cluster closest to the structure to create open space between them.
• Remove brush growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Cut grass around the structure short, especially during dry periods.
• Clear shrubs and low vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway to keep it passable.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Separate shrubs from one another where they grow in connected patches near the structure.
• Remove dead or dry ground vegetation beneath trees near the structure.
• Keep the area between the tree cluster and the structure free of shrubs and low growth that could carry fire toward the building.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation in the open areas nearest the structure regularly to keep it low.
